answer: Price new seats on a curve that climbs with the recent join rate. At the usual trickle a seat costs seconds of hashing; when one hour brings a flood, each extra identity costs more. An operator who wants to pour an ocean of clones into one epoch to sway the verdict on a rival's dune-migration survey pays steeply for every account in the tail. Spreading joins over months dodges the surge price, but then each clone must keep an unbroken thread of graded answers the whole time, so cheap mass identities stop existing.
